Diagnosis: Paget disease of the right nipple, s/p central lumpectomy 01/19/2023, margins negative, no underlying carcinoma.
Treatment: whole-breast radiation, right breast, 02/27/2023 - 04/07/2023, completed as planned without breaks.

documents.body:
CC: bleeding.
Postmenopausal (LMP early 50s). Since about May she has had irregular light vaginal bleeding on and off and spotting after intercourse. No pain. Didn't mention it at the wellness visit because she thought it was from "the radiation or the stress." Getting a little heavier lately.
Exam: abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic deferred to gynecology today at her request.
A/P: Postmenopausal bleeding with postcoital spotting - needs prompt gynecologic evaluation (exam, cervical assessment, endometrial evaluation). Referral placed, flagged for a visit within a few weeks. Bleeding precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/24/2023

59-year-old postmenopausal woman, referred for six months of irregular vaginal bleeding and postcoital spotting. Painless, but heavier over the last two months. She cannot recall a Pap test in more than ten years. Background: type 2 diabetes (poorly controlled), rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisone, hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine, iron deficiency anemia, Paget disease of the right nipple treated this year. NKDA. Smoker, 30 pack-years. Family: maternal aunt breast cancer at 62.

Vitals: within normal limits.
Pelvic exam: 3 cm exophytic lesion arising from the anterior lip of the cervix, friable, bleeding readily when touched. Vaginal walls free of tumor. Parametria soft and free on rectovaginal exam.
Labs: hemoglobin 10.2, WBC 7.0, platelets 250.
Procedure: cervical biopsy of the lesion; hemostasis with silver nitrate.

Impression: Gross cervical lesion highly suspicious for carcinoma. Pathology pending; will refer on to gynecologic oncology if confirmed.

reports.text: Specimen: cervix, anterior lip, biopsy. Sheets and nests of atypical squamous cells with keratinization infiltrating the stroma.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix.

documents.title: Telephone Encounter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Janet after receiving the gynecology letter and biopsy result. She had heard from the gynecologist on Friday. Tearful but has her sister with her. Gyn-onc appointment set for 12/14. Answered questions about next steps (imaging, then surgery vs radiation decided by the oncologist). Offered a visit any time; she'll message after the oncology visit. Reminded her the anemia is likely partly from the bleeding - keep the iron.

reports.text: CT chest with contrast for staging. No pulmonary nodules or masses. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Post-surgical change of the right breast. No pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Cervix mildly enlarged without extension into the parametria. No pelvic or para-aortic lymphadenopathy. Kidneys normal without hydronephrosis. Liver, spleen, adrenals and pancreas unremarkable. Sigmoid diverticulosis without inflammation. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: No adenopathy or distant metastatic disease.

OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - NEW CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/14/2023
Diagnosis: invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, biopsy 11/24/2023.
Exam under good light today: 3 cm exophytic anterior-lip lesion confined to the cervix. Vagina and parametria uninvolved.
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 12/11/2023: no adenopathy, no distant disease.
Clinical FIGO stage IB2.
Options discussed: radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy versus primary chemoradiation. She chose surgery. Planned open radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection, January 2024. Please provide medical optimization; A1c and smoking reduction would help healing. NKDA.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVAL - open radical hysterectomy/BSO/pelvic node dissection 1/17 (gyn onc).
Cervical SCC stage IB2, CT negative for spread. Bleeding lighter since biopsy.
Functional status good (>4 METs). No cardiac sx. ECG 12/2022 normal.
Exam: NAD. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Trace ankle edema. Abd soft.
Labs today: BMP, CBC (anemia known; Hb 10.2 on 11/24), A1c.
Assessment: Intermediate-risk open abdominal surgery in a patient with insulin-treated diabetes, chronic steroid use, smoking. No further cardiac testing indicated.
Recs:
- Glargine 16 units night before; hold metformin day of surgery and until eating; inpatient glucose protocol.
- Perioperative stress-dose steroids (on prednisone 5 mg >10 yrs).
- Methotrexate: discuss holding 1 week before/after with rheumatology and surgeon.
- Hold HCTZ day of surgery.
- VTE prophylaxis per surgical team.
- Continue iron.
- Stop smoking - she has cut to half a pack.

OUTSIDE HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 4 weeks after discharge)
Admitted 01/17/2024. Discharged 01/21/2024.
Procedure 01/17/2024: open radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection. EBL 450 mL. No transfusion.
Course: uncomplicated. Stress-dose hydrocortisone perioperatively, back to prednisone 5 mg on day 2. Glucose managed with basal insulin and correction scale. Foley removed day 3 with successful void.
Pathology: see report - stage IB2, node negative, margins negative, no LVSI.
Plan: no adjuvant therapy. Surveillance visits every 3-6 months with gynecologic oncology. Resume home medications. Allergies: NKDA.

CC: tired, bloated, legs more swollen.
For about six months: steadily more fatigue, abdomen feels bloated and full, and the swelling, which used to stop at the ankles, now comes up to her knees. Pants tight at the waist. No chest pain, no orthopnea. Urine looks foamy at times. No hematuria. No change in bowels.
Exam: Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no JVD. Abdomen soft, mildly distended, nontender. 2+ pitting edema to the knees bilaterally. Weight up ~2 kg.
Labs drawn at the visit, back this afternoon: UACR 3150 mg/g (was normal yearly through 10/2023). Albumin 3.0. Cr 1.1. UA protein 3+.
A/P:
1. Heavy proteinuria with low albumin and edema - nephrotic picture, new since last year. Diabetic kidney disease possible but the rapid change and RA history raise other causes. Urgent nephrology referral placed; called their office for a November slot.
2. Edema now beyond the amlodipine pattern. Leg elevation; no diuretic change pending nephrology.
3. Fatigue - likely related.

reports.text: Specimen: abdominal subcutaneous fat, aspiration/biopsy. Deposits of amorphous eosinophilic hyaline material. Congo red stain positive with apple-green birefringence under polarized light. Immunohistochemistry: amyloid deposits positive for serum amyloid A.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/29/2024

Thank you for sending Ms. Krause. She describes half a year of gradually worsening tiredness, a bloated abdomen and swelling of both legs. Background includes seropositive rheumatoid arthritis for over 20 years, treated with methotrexate and low-dose prednisone for roughly 15 of them, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, amlodipine-related ankle edema, iron deficiency anemia, Paget disease of the right nipple (2023) and stage IB2 cervical cancer (2024), both treated.

Medications: amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg bid, insulin glargine 20 units, ferrous sulfate, folic acid (plus methotrexate and prednisone as above). NKDA.

Exam: BP 140/90. 2+ pitting edema to the knees.

Results: albumin 2.8 g/dL; creatinine 1.2 mg/dL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; urine microscopy bland, no cells or casts; CRP 25 mg/L. Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation: no monoclonal protein.
Echocardiogram: normal LV function, no valve disease.
Abdominal fat pad biopsy: amorphous hyaline deposits, Congo red positive with apple-green birefringence; immunohistochemistry positive for serum amyloid A.

Impression: AA (secondary) amyloidosis from long-standing rheumatoid arthritis, with nephrotic-range proteinuria. No cardiac involvement on echo. No monoclonal protein to suggest AL.

Plan:
1. Losartan 25 mg daily started for proteinuria; BMP in 2 weeks - please draw at your office.
2. The key treatment is suppressing the inflammation driving amyloid production. I have written to her rheumatologist recommending escalation of RA therapy; an IL-6 receptor blocker is the usual choice.
3. Low-salt diet. Will see her again in 3 months.
